A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–B support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original estimates of redundancy between linguistic context and six prosodic features using LibriTTS, including context-length results and appendix distribution summaries.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Figures 1 and 3 and Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same feature-extraction pipeline, Gaussian kernel density estimator, and language models predicting conditional-distribution parameters from restricted contexts. The training objective, model candidates, and 1–10-word input spans are retained; added explanations do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same English LibriTTS audiobook data and six prosodic features. v3 discusses cross-language generalization but does not add languages, datasets, or evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: The BERT, BERT-large, and RoBERTa-large candidates and the long-context reference lines remain unchanged. v3 explicitly attributes those reference lines to Wolf et al. (2023), identifying an existing comparison rather than adding one.

E3.justification: Figure 3 changes the stated averaging population from 'all train data' to 'all test data', correcting the reported evaluation setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. The Section 4.1 splits and sample counts remain unchanged. The revised 0–9 context description clarifies counting around the target word rather than demonstrating changed input lengths.

E4.justification: The context-length analyses, individual-feature comparisons, and Appendix B histograms are retained. New discussion of correlations and possible confounds is not accompanied by new ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors of the mean in Figure 3 and distribution means and standard deviations in Figure 4. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: The underlying MI heatmaps, feature-level trends, six unconditional entropies in Table 1, and histogram summary statistics are unchanged. Both retain the main 3–8-word past versus 1–2-word future finding and the duration/pause exceptions. Figure redesigns do not introduce new results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the mutual-information formulation, cross-entropy approximation, context definition, and monotonicity argument are retained. v3 adds explanatory wording but no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central empirical contribution remains unchanged. However, Hypothesis 2 changes from a timescale short relative to the past to an explicit 1–2-word prediction, and the abstract newly foregrounds consistency with incremental language-production planning.

C2.justification: The future-context rationale shifts from audience-oriented prediction toward incremental production planning. v3 also substantially expands qualifications: correlated features are modeled separately, the stressed-syllable pitch window may underrepresent boundary tones, retained capitalization can expose sentence boundaries, and audiobook syntax and English-only coverage constrain interpretation. These changes materially broaden the explanation and applicability boundaries of the retained findings.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents equal sample counts across context combinations, retained capitalization, and CELEX as the source of syllable counts, while expanding feature-extraction explanations. It also describes the linked pipeline as publicly available instead of promising release. These are documentation and availability-statement changes, not evidence of a modified implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds supporting literature on incremental production, comprehension, neural integration, and prosodic typology, including Bock et al., Brown-Schmidt and Konopka, Botch and Finn, and Wilcox et al.; the Cowan reference is removed. The central positioning as a context-length extension of Wolf et al. (2023) remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the feature descriptions, methods, results, and discussion are rewritten or expanded. Methodological footnotes are incorporated into the main text, terminology and author information are corrected, and acknowledgments are added. This is extensive narrative revision despite retaining the overall section structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces cell-number annotations with outlined hypothesis-testing regions and an exploratory-region label. Figure 3 rearranges panels and revises axes, legends, and captions; Figure 4 similarly reorganizes and relabels the distributions and explains their units. Together these substantially revise the presentation of the main and appendix figures while retaining their data.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity and transparency through clearer hypothesis framing, more informative figure captions, the train/test caption correction, and substantive discussion of measurement and generalization limits. Figure 1 trades printed cell values for clearer hypothesis annotations, while feature-level values remain in Figure 3. The empirical evidence and underlying estimation limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited rather than a substantial strengthening of the study.
